name: GitHub
description: Issues, pull requests, code search and reviews on the repositories you can reach.
long_description:
GitHub's own hosted MCP server. It reads and writes issues, pull requests, files, workflows and releases, using your GitHub account's permissions — it can reach exactly what you can reach, and nothing more.

There are two ways in. **Sign in** needs a GitHub OAuth application with Device Flow enabled: GitHub registers no client automatically and refuses a redirect sign-in without a client secret, so Gantry asks the server for a code and you approve it on github.com. **Use a token** takes a fine-grained personal access token instead and needs no application at all.

Whichever you choose, the credential is encrypted on this machine and is never sent anywhere except to GitHub.

auth.instructions: GitHub registers no application on its own, and it will not take one without a secret — so Gantry signs in with a code instead. Create an app (the button fills the form in), tick **Enable Device Flow** in its settings, and paste its Client ID here. This happens once.

auth_alternate.instructions: Create a fine-grained token with access to the repositories you want, then paste it here. Nothing to register, nothing to tick.

risk.notes: Acts as you on GitHub. Merging, force-pushing and deleting are asked about every time.
